newsitem.title: GERMANY: DHL sees 20-25pct Europe growth up to 2000.
newsitem.headline: DHL sees 20-25pct Europe growth up to 2000.

text.p: Global express freight company DHL International said it foresees 20-25 percent annual growth in Europe up to 2000.

Rainer Butz, DHL director strategic alliances, said large-scale investment in information technology and Internet use would be part of a gradual "evolution" of the company's services over the coming years.

"If the globalisation of companies is successful, then I believe growth rates (for DHL) of 20-25 percent are possible. For documents, it will be less, about 10 percent," he said in a speech to the third European courier, express and parcels congress here.
DHL handled 60 percent of its European freight, or 157,000 tonnes, last year at its Brussels hub, with the remaining 40 percent handled at nine sub-hubs, he noted.
Butz said DHL planned to invest 450-600 million marks a year in Europe over the coming three years.
Information technology would alone account for 120 million marks a year of this investment, he noted.
"What (freight) integrators have done with their infrastructure was a revolution and now there will be an evolution at a high level," he said.

The top DHL priority in Europe would be to improve quality of performance and service and expand capacity so that DHL could cope with short-term peaks in demand caused by strikes or other events, he added.
In its Internet home page, DHL planned to give clients the option of naming delivery locations, Butz said.
The company expected to see a general growth in electronic commerce in the coming years, he added.
